title: Forgetting under noise is undecidable
description: A natural noisy Wang rule on Z^4 is ergodic exactly when its finite raw tile set does not tile the plane. A cardinal checker and a fixed 512-of-768 quorum use the tiles themselves and one blank. A transverse-quorum lift of Kari's nilpotency reduction gives the same equivalence on Z^3 for north/east deterministic tile sets. One explicit positive rational replacement rate, independent of the input, makes ergodicity undecidable in both families. For non-tiling inputs, amortized coherence and an all-path density lemma prove finite-window coupling from the past for all starts; tiling gives two invariant laws. A saturation theorem explains why the earlier budget-only estimate needs six dimensions. The retained Z^6 natural rule has exponential all-input coalescence with a universal computable slope and uncomputable delay, all-Gibbs uniqueness and robustness. Its Theorems D and A are verified in Lean; the Z^4 and Z^3 results are not formalized. The inspector theory and Z^8 machine-family Lean core are retained.
notes: Preprint. It has not been peer reviewed. Version 2.0.0 restructures the paper around a natural rule applied directly to raw Wang sets: on Z^6 it is ergodic at every rate up to (2(18q)^2)^(-200), q = 5*16^4, exactly when the tile set does not tile the plane (Theorem D), which gives fixed-rate undecidability on Z^6 (Theorem A). New in this version: Theorem E, the natural rule on Z^4 for every raw Wang set, and Theorem F, fixed-rate undecidability on Z^3 for north/east-deterministic tile sets (a transverse-quorum lift of Kari's 1992 nilpotency reduction), both at every rate up to 382205952^(-33720); a saturation theorem explaining why the earlier coherence estimate needs six dimensions; and the consequences of Theorem D. Theorem D, Theorem A on Z^6, the domino reduction and the undecidability of the domino problem are proved in Lean 4 with no named hypotheses (lean-natural/); the Z^8 machine-family core of version 1.4.0 is kept in lean/. Every proved statement of version 1.4.0 is kept; the old Theorem A on Z^8 is now the machine-family theorem. Updates version 1.4.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24126025). Text: CC BY 4.0.
